messages.content: Can you find the fastest route from my home in San Francisco to my office in Palo Alto, then from my office to my friend's house in San Jose, and finally from my friend's house back to my home, while avoiding toll roads?

function.name: map_routing_fastest_route
function.description: Finds the fastest route from one location to another, with an option to avoid toll roads. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

start_location.description: The starting location for the journey.

avoid_tolls.description: Option to avoid toll roads during the journey. default is False

message.reasoning:
The user wants three legs:

1) SF (home) -> Palo Alto (office)
2) Palo Alto -> San José (friend's house)
3) San José -> SF (back home)

Avoid tolls.

We need to call the routing tool multiple times or combine into single multi-stop? The function only supports start/end; no waypoints. So we can do separate calls per leg.

We'll produce output summarizing each leg with distance/time maybe. But the function returns "any" - unknown format. We should just pass arguments accordingly.

Thus we will make three calls to `map_routing_fastest_route` with appropriate parameters.

Let's craft JSON calls.

First leg: start="San Francisco", end="Palo Alto", avoid_tolls=true.

Second: start="Palo Alto", end="San Jose", avoid_tolls=true.

Third: start="San Jose", end="San Francisco", avoid_tolls=true.

Return results aggregated.

Ok let's proceed.
